notes: Read the single source line with its line number before porting. web L1 is a pure re-export barrel: `export { LiveSignalsTable } from './LiveSignalsTable';`. The native port keeps it a pure barrel and imports no DOM modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, or old web UI components.

The one exported symbol, LiveSignalsTable (web L1), maps to a sibling module that has NOT yet been ported into the native parity tree (apps/native/src/web-parity/features/admin/components/live-signal-inspector contained no LiveSignalsTable, and the table's DataTable/Input/useSortToggle/Column/TimeStamp building blocks are likewise unported). Re-exporting it would point at a missing file and break `tsc --noEmit`, so per the established native-barrel convention it is enumerated in nativeLiveSignalInspectorBarrelCapabilities.pending.exports with a shared NATIVE_LIVE_SIGNAL_INSPECTOR_PENDING_REASON, giving an explicit unavailable state that keeps the source public API documented and discoverable. This mirrors the native feedback barrel (nativeFeedbackBarrelCapabilities) and charts barrel (nativeChartsBarrelCapabilities).

No native consumer currently imports LiveSignalsTable / live-signal-inspector (verified by grep across apps/native/src), so deferring the symbol breaks nothing; the web consumer LiveSignalInspectorPage.tsx is a separate, not-yet-ported file. When the loop converts LiveSignalsTable this barrel will be revisited and the symbol promoted from `pending` to a live re-export, exactly as Skeleton was promoted in the native feedback barrel.

The barrel carries no behavior, state names, API paths, unit handling, or i18n strings of its own beyond module re-export wiring, so there is nothing runtime to preserve; the deferred re-export is faithfully reproduced as an explicit pending capability record. The trailing newline carries no export and needs no port.
